summary: This aluminum foundry released about 3,700 lb to the air in 2024, mostly the solvent tetrachloroethylene.

impacts.title: Air & breathing
impacts.where: North side of Manitowoc, within 1 mile: 3,747 residents
impacts.how: About 2,600 lb of tetrachloroethylene, which EPA lists as likely to cause cancer, went into the air, plus 500 lb of formaldehyde and small amounts of nickel. Both solvents irritate the eyes and lungs.

avoid.label: Check air quality
avoid.text: Check the daily air quality index (AirNow), especially on hot, still days

avoid.label: Report odors
avoid.text: Report strong or unusual odors in the forum, where the company can reply. You can also call the DNR tip line, 1-800-847-9367

avoid.label: Comment on permits
avoid.text: Comment on the plant's air permit when the DNR opens it for public input

impacts.title: Seniors & schools
impacts.where: 23% of nearby residents are seniors; 4 schools within 1 mile
impacts.how: This neighborhood has Manitowoc's highest share of older residents, who are more sensitive to air pollution, along with four schools.

avoid.label: Limit time outside
avoid.text: Older adults with heart or lung disease should limit time outdoors on poor-air days

avoid.label: Ask your school
avoid.text: Ask schools whether they track the air quality index

avoid.label: Join hearings
avoid.text: Join DNR public hearings, like the one held in 2023 on the foundry's new furnaces

impacts.title: Groundwater
impacts.how: Tetrachloroethylene lasts a long time in groundwater wherever it reaches the soil. It's released here to the air, so this is a possible pathway rather than a confirmed one.

avoid.label: Test your well
avoid.text: If you use a private well, test it for volatile organic compounds (VOCs)

avoid.label: City water is lake water
avoid.text: City water users are on Lake Michigan water

avoid.label: Report spills
avoid.text: Report spills or strong solvent smells in the forum. If one is happening now, call the DNR 24-hour spill line, 1-800-943-0003, first
